hooks.text: A dead star is slowly vaporizing its own companion into thin air.
Every 1.6 milliseconds, this dead star pulses while destroying its partner.
The companion star did not explode; it is being eaten alive.

title: The Dead Star That Eats Its Companion
description: Astronomers discovered a cannibalistic pulsar that slowly destroys its own partner star through a relentless beam of high-energy radiation.

beats.text: A dead star is slowly vaporizing its own companion into thin air.
beats.visual: Artist impression of a black widow pulsar evaporating its companion star, 2012
queries: artist impression of binary star system

beats.text: In 1988, astronomers discovered PSR B1957+20, a rapidly spinning neutron star in our Milky Way galaxy.
beats.visual: Palomar Observatory Samuel Oschin Telescope dome, 1948

beats.text: The pulsar rotates once every 1.6 milliseconds, while its companion star completes an entire orbit in just 9.2 hours.
beats.visual: Diagram of millisecond pulsar binary Roche lobe accretion and ablation

beats.text: As the pulsar races through space at nearly one million kilometers per hour, it generates a supersonic bow shock.
beats.visual: Artist concept illustration of the bow shock created by PSR B1957+20

beats.text: The pulsar relentlessly blasts this companion with high-energy radiation, stripping away its outer layers until nothing remains.
Fermi data confirms this 1.8 solar mass beast grew by consuming its partner's material.
This destructive system earned the nickname black widow, named for the spider species known for killing its mate.
beats.visual: Artist impression of a black widow pulsar evaporating its companion star, 2012

better_than_last: Resolved the dangling sentence ending in the final beat by completing the thought with the spider namesake, creating a grammatically complete and seamless loop back to the hook.
